title.narrative: Support to Strengthening the Capacities of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre, Maritime Safety and Security and Law Enforcement to Counter Maritime Crime in Maldives

description.narrative:
The Global Maritime Crime Programme (GMCP) of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
supports Member States in strengthening its capacities in enhancing and coordinating their efforts against maritime
crime. Maldives is an archipelagic state with a population of around 515,000 people and located in the Indian
Ocean, in one of the main trade routes in the world. Around 20,000 vessels travel through the Maldives every day,
having its territorial waters as a major transportation route for oil and petroleum products. However, criminal
networks also use these waters to carry out illicit activities, including illegal fishing and drug smuggling. Both
maritime law enforcement as well as ensuring maritime safety and timely response to major incidents have
remained a challenge for years. The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (hereinafter MRCC) under Maldives
National Defence Force is responsible for receiving reports on maritime accidents, incidents and search and rescue
operations, and coordinating law enforcement activities. As of today, the size of the MRCC building is only 28
square metres and has no adequate space for telecommunications equipment, operational function nor training.
Hence, under this project, GMCP intends to procure 450,000 USD worth of construction material to complete the
building for MRCC which will enhance overall capacity building of the Government of Maldives in incident
preparedness and response to the threats and challenges of search and rescue, and maritime law enforcement
operations to disrupt maritime crime.
